newsitem.title: USA: Wash. 1,158 MW nuclear unit outage delayed to Wed.
newsitem.headline: Wash. 1,158 MW nuclear unit outage delayed to Wed.

text.p: The 1,158 megawatt (MW) WNP-2 nuclear power unit will begin its annual outage on Wednesday rather than Saturday as previously expected, a spokesman for the plant said Friday.
"We wanted a few extra days to be sure that repairs to our adjustable speed drive" were adequate, he noted.
WNP-2 operations have fluctuated since early January due to problems with the speed drive as well as Bonneville Power Administration's (BPA) supply needs.
BPA said earlier this week the nuclear plant would shut Saturday until early July due to a regional abundance of lower-cost hydropower.
But the plan now is for WNP-2 to go off-line Wednesday evening.
The plant is now at 100 percent, but will drop to 55 percent around midnight through 0200 PST on Monday, when it will power up to 100 percent by 0800 PST.
WNP-2 will maintain full operations until 2200 PST on Monday, dropping to 90 percent until Tuesday morning at 0800 PST, when it will return to 100 percent.
WNP-2 will continue running at full capacity during the day and 90 percent at night until 2000 PST on Wednesday, when it will begin moving into cold shutdown.
